gap: No result ChatGPT got states the 18.5-inch class priced side by side from the makers' own US stores on one date: Aura's three-screen Triple Boost Pro Studio 18.5" is $579 and its Triple Aero Pro Studio 18.5" is $629 (ChatGPT's cards said $629 and $699), UPERFECT's own store marks the dual 18.5" Delta Max (ChatGPT's top pick) unavailable at $499.99, and all four Aura 18.5" models need a driver install.
standout_why: Compared against theofficejournal.com (attachable guide), itechguides.com (15 extenders, first 100,000 characters), twelvetabs.com and deal.ai. The first three name no 18-inch or 18.5-inch model at all; their largest screens are 16 to 16.1 inches. deal.ai prices only the INVZI MagHub Quad Max ($899.99 Best Buy, $999.00 INVZI, both checked Nov 19) against a 16-inch UPERFECT. None gives maker-store prices for the Aura 18.5" range, the UPERFECT Delta Max stock status, or the driver requirement across the class. It stops short of 3 because I could not open the Newegg listing behind ChatGPT's $399.99 UPERFECT card, nor the FOPO S999 page for its video path.
decides: It changes the pick. For three added 18.5" screens, Aura's Triple Boost Pro Studio at $579 beats our only 18.5" candidate, the FOPO S999 at $1,099.99 (no record yet), by $520.99, so the S999 cannot honestly win on price. ChatGPT's top pick, the UPERFECT dual, is unavailable at the maker's store, which leaves Aura's Dual Boost Pro Studio 18.5" at $489 as the dual I could price in stock. The page reaches two linked rows only if an S999 record is added alongside the FOPO S788, which has 16-inch screens and qualifies only if the question means an extender for an 18-inch laptop (FOPO's stated fit range is 12–18.5-inch laptops). If the S999 row is not wanted, the page is a skip.
